# Current owner-update kernel maintainability audit

Read-only inspection of the integrated source against `.cache/owner-update-kernel-primary-integration/before` and `.cache/runtime-simplification-review/plan.md`. No source or test files were changed and no tests were run. This is a structure review, not a latency assessment.

## State ownership and duplicated representations

- **World is authoritative for committed state.** `OwnerStateWorld` owns each cell’s value/version, cell identity, owner/site, layout, lane, row lease and generation. `numericLaneForCell` resolves a capability plus captured version and validates the lane at [owner_state_world.ts](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:1711); `numericRowForCell` additionally cross-checks the cached row view against the exact lease, layout, source, slot, row and generation at [owner_state_world.ts](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:1736). The kernel did not add a second mutable World cell table or a World-to-VDOM dependency.
- **Compiler metadata is static; its association cache is derived.** `compiled_state_layout.ts` now uses one `WeakMap` record for normalized layout, signature, lazy slot lookup and the optional immutable owner program ([compiled_state_layout.ts](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/compiled_state_layout.ts:54), [association](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/compiled_state_layout.ts:140)). This replaces the three-cache duplication identified in the earlier simplification plan. The owner program is validated against the same `programId` and slot count and is resolved during row preparation, not per cut.
- **VDOM prepared rows hold revocable snapshots and host state.** Each record keeps World vector leases alongside its local source/column references, layout signature, used slots, fanout groups, captured inputs, duplicate/conflict epochs and active state ([record](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:103)). Those lease and identity snapshots are independent checks, not accidental copies: execution verifies caller vectors still match before mirroring source values ([preflight](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3328)). The added `sinks` list maps compiler sink order to existing `BoundPropGroup`s while `groupsBySlot` preserves the fallback’s slot fanout order; they are duplicate references serving different traversal orders.
- **Root has three strategy layers.** It captures native handles/versions, tries prepared row tokens first, prepared lane tokens second, then existing scalar-source program fallback ([row route](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/component_state_runtime.ts:4863), [lane route](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/component_state_runtime.ts:4968), [selection](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/component_state_runtime.ts:5095)). The caches/scratch overlap in publication, `lastSourceValues`, acknowledgement, decline/retry and cleanup, but the row route validates layout/row membership while the lane route supports the narrower lane-backed scalar case. Removing one route is not a safe cleanup until a compatibility inventory proves the other route or generic fallback covers every legacy and promoted case.

## What changed and what remains

The preserved pre-kernel VDOM had prepared-row capture/mirroring followed by dynamic slot fanout, sink deduplication, input-vector copies, projector callbacks, equality and ordered writes. The current row record optionally associates an owner kernel during preparation after checking complete sink IDs and matching per-slot fanout order ([eligibility](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:2505)). At execution, the entire cut is captured and validated, then either every row uses the same kernel or the whole cut uses the generic executor; source mirrors still precede all projection, and all projection still precedes host writes ([selection and execution](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3376), [phase boundary](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3437)). Kernel outputs are validated before host writes; VDOM retains host publication, cancellation, value caches, and cleanup.

The new private Rust module `owner_update_program.rs` isolates expression whitelist parsing, identifier-span rewriting to `rowState.inputValues[slot]`, and generated switch/fanout body construction ([owner_update_program.rs](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/compiler/oxc-spike/src/owner_update_program.rs:24), [emission](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/compiler/oxc-spike/src/owner_update_program.rs:115)). This is a useful module boundary for AST-specific code. It does **not** own certification, cross-sink ineligibility, stable program/sink identity, component grouping, runtime metadata registration or fallback selection; those remain in `main.rs` ([certification](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/compiler/oxc-spike/src/main.rs:3323), [owner grouping](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/compiler/oxc-spike/src/main.rs:3731), [descriptor registration](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/compiler/oxc-spike/src/main.rs:3820)). The module isolates one coherent expression-rewriting concern; it does not substantially shrink the compiler’s classification/control-flow surface or the runtime’s state coordination. Line count alone would overstate simplification.

The kernel reduced one generic execution representation: groups on a kernel-capable row no longer eagerly allocate `ownerRowInputs`; those vectors are allocated only if a later heterogeneous/unsupported cut needs the generic fallback ([row setup](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:2600), [fallback setup](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3416)). The per-group projector/slot metadata stays because fallback semantics remain live. This is a real memory-path reduction for eligible rows, alongside a new kernel path and new staged output scratch; no broad Root/VDOM complexity reduction follows from it.

## Branching, lifetime and comments

1. Compiler eligibility is conservative: candidate expressions must be owner-local, immutable, numeric-state-only and pass the existing purity scan; unqualified candidates stay on fallback ([main.rs](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/compiler/oxc-spike/src/main.rs:3372)). Kernel lowering separately parses a strict syntax whitelist; calls, member reads, assignments, arrays/objects and unknown forms remain v2 ([owner_update_program.rs](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/compiler/oxc-spike/src/owner_update_program.rs:29)). This conservative two-stage gate is intentional, although the distinction between *certified source* and *kernel-lowerable source* is not named explicitly at the call site.
2. VDOM preparation checks descriptor schema/program/slot count, maps unique runtime groups to compiler sink IDs, then confirms generated sink order matches every slot’s actual group fanout. Runtime execution additionally selects the kernel only for a homogeneous owner program and complete sink set; otherwise it initializes any missing fallback vectors and runs the established generic path. This is a meaningful preparation-time proof and execution-time whole-cut branch, not a per-sink alternate mixture.
3. VDOM terminal execution clears row/group/staged scratch prefixes in `finally` and releases high-water buffers on cancellation/disposal ([cleanup](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3568)). Root clears row tokens/views and numeric values after each accepted/declined row cut; disposal resets the strategy caches ([Root disposal](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/component_state_runtime.ts:2265)). These are separate lifetimes because Root owns captured World handles and VDOM owns projected host values.
4. The added comments observed in the reviewed kernel paths are short: the Rust whitelist explanation is two lines; VDOM/Root internal comments in the touched path are at most two lines. The exported layout/kernel contracts use short TSDoc. No comment wall or broad renaming is needed.

## Three bounded follow-ups

1. **Delete the redundant `seenMask` reset on VDOM epoch rollover.** The wrap branch resets `seenMask` for every active row at [vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3298), but every kernel-selected cut resets it again for each affected row immediately before invocation ([kernel setup](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3404)); no other use is present. Remove only the global wrap assignment after a focused forced-epoch test covering a wrapped cut, duplicate changed slots and both kernel and generic branches. Risk is low but test the wrapped transition because epoch rollover also resets other per-row/per-group dedup state.
2. **Name the compiler’s two eligibility stages without moving them.** At [main.rs](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/compiler/oxc-spike/src/main.rs:3323), `certified` means local source certification, while later `pure` additionally means none of the referenced sites was made ineligible by another candidate. The private lowering module can still reject syntax after both checks. Rename only these locals/fields to role names such as `source_certified` and `owner_kernel_eligible`; keep the checks in place. Add exact output-equivalence cases for overlapping candidates, out-of-owner reads and a locally pure but non-lowerable expression. This removes ambiguity without creating a compiler facade.
3. **Keep Root’s row and lane strategies separate for now; remove duplicated acceptance code only after a shared proof.** Their commit closures currently repeat decline-to-no-publication conversion, `lastSourceValues` writes, pending/World acknowledgements and counters. A later small extraction could share the post-acceptance publication tail while leaving row/lane preflight and retry preparation separate. The proof must cover accepted `false` (no host write but accepted cut), decline on both attempts (no publication/acknowledgement), captured values under reentry, disposed root and host failure. Do not merge token maps or strategies as an initial cleanup: their World proof boundaries differ.

The compiler’s prior unread `NativePropCandidate.state_ref_counts` item from the earlier plan is already absent in the current source; it should not be reported as an outstanding deletion. No performance or maintainability conclusion is inferred from tests or source line totals here.
